title: How do you build a training matrix for a construction company?
description: Build a construction training matrix: trades and supervisors against white cards, licences, SWMS, fall, scaffold, silica, crane and asbestos rules by market.
shortAnswer: A construction training matrix lists site roles such as laborers, scaffolders, crane operators, concrete cutters and supervisors against the obligations each market imposes: Australian white cards, high risk work licences, SWMS briefings and asbestos training; US OSHA fall protection, scaffold, silica and crane rules; and general duties in the EU, Portugal, Japan and Abu Dhabi. Each cell records the trigger, the renewal or retraining rule, and the evidence an inspector will ask for.
keyTakeaways: Construction obligations attach to tasks (working at height, cutting concrete, lifting, entering pits), so split broad trade titles into task based roles.

Only a few frequencies are fixed in law, such as the 5 year life of an Australian high risk work licence and US crane certification; most US construction retraining is triggered by change or poor performance.
Australian white cards have no printed expiry but stop counting after 2 years without construction work, so the matrix must track activity, not just the card.
Principal contractors need subcontractor rows: card and licence sighting, SWMS collection and site induction are their evidence, not the subcontractor's.
State the market on every row. A multi country builder runs different rules for the same task in Sydney, Texas, Lisbon, Osaka and Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: Why does a construction company need its own kind of training matrix?

blocks.text: Because construction obligations are triggered by the task a person does on a given day, not by their payroll title. A carpenter who spends a week on a roof edge, then cuts fiber cement, then helps strip a scaffold has picked up three separate sets of requirements. A generic [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) built on job titles misses that.

The second difference is the workforce. Most people on a construction site are employed by someone other than the principal contractor, so the matrix has to show what the builder checked, not only what its own employees completed. The third is that licenses and cards are issued by regulators and training organizations outside the company, which means expiry and validity rules sit outside the company's control and must be tracked rather than set.

sections.heading: Which regulations feed a construction training matrix?

blocks.text: In practice, the obligations come from each market's construction specific rules plus its general duty to train. The table lists the sources documented in this library, as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Which roles belong on the vertical axis?

blocks.text: List roles by the hazardous tasks they perform, then add the supervisory and site management roles that carry distinct duties. A useful construction role list usually includes the following.

items: **Any person doing construction work**, including engineers, surveyors and managers who enter the site, because the Australian white card applies to all of them.
**Workers at height**: roofers, framers, leading edge and facade workers.
**Scaffold users** and, separately, **scaffold erectors and inspectors**, since OSHA sets different trainers and content for each group.
**Lifting crew**: crane operators, operators in training, doggers and riggers.
**Concrete and masonry cutters**, for silica exposure.
**Trades who may disturb asbestos**, such as plumbers, electricians and demolition crew, and **licensed removal workers and supervisors** as a separate role.
**Confined space entrants, attendants, entry supervisors and rescuers.**
**Supervisors, leading hands and foremen**, who enforce SWMS and, in Japan, receive foreman education.
**Site managers for the principal contractor**, who own subcontractor checks.
**First aiders, health and safety representatives and emergency wardens.**

blocks.text: Defining roles this way is a form of [job task analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-job-task-analysis): the task list, not the trade name, decides the requirements.

sections.heading: What does a construction training matrix look like in practice?

Frequencies marked as fixed come from the cited rules; the rest are trigger based.

sections.heading: Which refresh intervals are fixed and which are triggered?

blocks.text: Most construction refresher rules are triggered by change or poor performance, and only a handful set a calendar interval. Treat the two differently: fixed intervals drive due dates, triggers need an event feed.

items: **Fixed.** Australian high risk work licences expire 5 years after grant (model WHS Regulations r 92). US crane operator certification is valid 5 years (29 CFR 1926.1427(d) and (e)). US confined space rescuers practice at least every 12 months (1926.1211(b)(4)). The written silica exposure control plan is reviewed at least annually (1926.1153(g)(2)). The model first aid Code recommends annual CPR refreshers and requalification every 3 years.

**Triggered by change.** OSHA fall protection retraining follows workplace changes, changes in systems or equipment, or gaps in knowledge or use (1926.503(c)). Scaffold retraining follows worksite or equipment changes or inadequate performance (1926.454(c)). Australian SWMS are reviewed when control measures are revised (r 302). The EU Framework Directive's Article 12 lists recruitment, transfer or change of job, new or changed equipment and new technology.

**Triggered by inactivity.** The Australian white card has no printed expiry, but a worker whose training is more than 2 years old and who has not done construction work in the preceding 2 years must be retrained (r 316).

blocks.text: For the reasoning behind choosing intervals where the law is silent, see [mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: How should a principal contractor record subcontractor competence?

blocks.text: By giving subcontractor workers their own rows, with evidence rules that describe what the principal contractor saw. Under the model WHS Regulations, a construction project is work costing $250,000 or more (r 292), and the principal contractor must obtain SWMS before high risk construction work starts (r 312).

items: Collect each subcontractor's SWMS and record the version against the activity.
Sight white cards; a worker who has applied but not received one may present certification issued within the preceding 60 days (r 317(2)).
Sight high risk work licences and keep the record for at least 1 year (r 85).
Deliver the site specific induction and record it separately from the white card, which covers general content only.
Recheck at each mobilization rather than once per contract, because cards lapse through inactivity and licences expire.

blocks.title: Australian currency note
blocks.text: The model WHS laws apply in every Australian jurisdiction except Victoria, which has its own Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 with an equivalent duty to train. Check local adoption before relying on a model regulation number.

sections.heading: What evidence will a construction inspector ask to see?

blocks.text: Inspectors ask for the record each rule prescribes, so the matrix's evidence column should copy the rule's own fields. Completion alone rarely satisfies them.

items: OSHA fall protection: a written certification with the employee's name, training dates and the trainer's or employer's signature, keeping the latest one (1926.503(b)).
OSHA silica: each employee must be able to demonstrate knowledge of the listed topics, which points to an assessed check rather than attendance (1926.1153(i)(2)).
OSHA cranes: a certificate does not by itself make an operator qualified; the employer's evaluation must also be documented (1926.1427(f)).
US confined spaces in construction: records with employee and trainer names and dates, kept for the period of employment (1926.1207(d)). Australian confined space training records: 2 years (r 76(2)).
Australian asbestos: training records for 5 years after the worker stops the work (r 445(3)), and licensed removal records accessible at the removal area (r 461).
Japan: special education records kept for 3 years under Ordinance article 38.

blocks.text: OSHA's preliminary FY 2026 top ten most cited standards place 1926.501 duty to have fall protection first and the 1926.503 training requirement eighth, which is why the fall protection cell deserves the strictest evidence rule. See [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How do language rules change the matrix?

blocks.text: They add an understanding requirement to cells that might otherwise accept a signature. Construction crews are often multilingual, and several markets say so directly.

items: Safe Work Australia's SWMS information sheet says a SWMS must be easily understood, including by workers from non English speaking backgrounds.
OSHA's 2010 Training Standards Policy Statement says training means presenting information in a manner employees can understand, including language and vocabulary.
ADOSH-SF Element 1 requires information, instruction, training and supervision in appropriate languages.
Under the model Code of Practice on managing WHS risks, a signed acknowledgment of a procedure is not enough on its own to show a worker has been trained.

blocks.text: Record the language of delivery in the evidence column for SWMS briefings and heat training.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each construction obligation as a requirement linked to its source clause, the task based roles it applies to, and the evidence rule that proves it, so a SWMS revision or a regulatory change flags the affected cells. See [gap analysis](/platform/gap-analysis).

faqs.q: Does a white card ever expire?
faqs.a: The model WHS Regulations do not put an expiry date on the card. However, a business must not allow construction work by someone whose training is more than 2 years old if they have not done construction work in the preceding 2 years. SafeWork NSW describes the card as void in that situation.

faqs.q: Is an OSHA 10 or 30 hour Outreach card enough for OSHA construction training duties?
faqs.a: No. OSHA states that its Outreach Training Program is voluntary, does not meet the training requirements of any OSHA standard and is not a certification. Standard specific training, such as fall protection or scaffold training, still has to be provided and paid for by the employer.

faqs.q: Who should own the construction training matrix?
faqs.a: Usually the safety or operations function owns the rules, while each project's site manager owns subcontractor checks and status for people on that site. Officers have a role too: in Australia, due diligence under section 27(5) of the WHS Act includes taking reasonable steps to verify that resources and processes are provided and used.

faqs.q: Should psychosocial hazard training be a matrix row?
faqs.a: It can be, but it should not be the main control. Victoria's Psychological Health Regulations 2025 allow information, instruction or training to be relied on alone only where changing work design, systems or environment is not reasonably practicable. Record training as one control among several.
